newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU'S BIG THREE SHOULD GAIN MORE SAY - EUROCRAT.
newsitem.headline: EU'S BIG THREE SHOULD GAIN MORE SAY - EUROCRAT.

text.p: The European Union's foreign relations commissioner, Hans van den Broek, said on Saturday that smaller EU states should cede power to the 'Big Three' in the interests of faster decision-making.

France, Germany and Britain should be afforded greater powers in return for pledging a more pro-European foreign policy approach and agreeing to more decisions on the basis of qualified majority voting, news agency ANP quoted him as saying.
Van den Broek, a former Dutch foreign minister, was speaking in a personal capacity to a conference on the Dutch presidency of the European Union.
Europe is wrestling with the problem of how to make decision-making more efficient ahead of a further enlargement of the 15-nation alliance.
"These proposals will be sufficient to break through the current impasse," he said.

Under Van den Broek's proposal, smaller member states would lose the right to veto EU decisions, while Bonn, Paris and London could only block decisions through a joint veto together with another member of the 'Big Three'. 251538 GMT jan 97
